QX-THORNE.name: Polarized adjoint Bloch--Kato vanishing
QX-THORNE.reference: J.A.Thorne, arXiv:2207.04925, Theorem6.1, printedp24; unitary-adjoint normalization and delta^n epsilon^(1-n) in Section6.3, p25.
QX-THORNE.statement: For an actual regular algebraic cuspidal polarized pair over a CM field and n>=2, irreducibility on the full cyclotomic extension implies vanishing of its polarized adjoint H1_f.
QX-THORNE.matching: QX1 proves surjectivity onto Gamma-prime, actual Frobenius attachment, exact form scalar cancellation and minus-transpose action, finite coefficient capture and original Af.IsBK matching. No residual adequacy or lower bound on ell is inferred.

QX-BLGGT.name: Polarized Galois representations and algebraic Hecke avatars
QX-BLGGT.reference: Barnet-Lamb--Gee--Geraghty--Taylor, Annals179(2014), Theorem2.1.1(1)--(3), printedp538, and AppendixA.2, printedp600.
QX-BLGGT.statement: Actual regular algebraic polarized cusp pairs have continuous semisimple Galois representations with geometric local compatibility away ell and de Rham property. Algebraic ell-adic rank-one characters are the avatars of algebraic Hecke characters, with the explicit infinity/cyclotomic normalization.
QX-BLGGT.matching: QX1 uses the exact CSD polarization. QX7 checks integral local exponents before using rank-one reciprocity. QX9 first constructs and sign-corrects actual polarized pairs; no infinity sign is identified with the uncorrected avatar at complex conjugation.

QX-CHENEVIER.name: Determinants, integral coefficient identities and absolutely irreducible realization
QX-CHENEVIER.reference: G.Chenevier, arXiv:0809.0415v2, Lemma1.12, Corollary1.14, Theorem1.15, Theorem2.22(i), Remark3.5.
QX-CHENEVIER.statement: Integral mixed determinant coefficients are polynomials in group-word characteristic coefficients; a split absolutely irreducible residual Cayley--Hamilton determinant over a henselian ring is a matrix determinant; universal determinant rings are topologically generated by their coefficient functions.
QX-CHENEVIER.matching: QX3 applies to the dual-number point and upgrades weak Pair trace relations by Burnside/Nakayama. QX5 descends the full law integrally, including ell=3. QX3 does not apply B.univ to Qbar[epsilon].

QX-CFT.name: Finite and local class field theory
QX-CFT.reference: J.S.Milne, Class Field Theory v4.03, I Theorems1.1,1.4; V Theorems5.3,5.5 and Remark5.7.
QX-CFT.statement: Local units correspond to inertia; global finite abelian extensions and ray-class characters are given by idele reciprocity with compatible norms and Frobenius.
QX-CFT.matching: QX4 explicitly constructs kappa0 and the one-sided ell-adic character mu using finite ray classes; the root/continuity/parity/threshold calculations are proved. QX7 and QX9 use the original local embeddings and finite coefficient fields.

QX-CHEBOTAREV.name: Chebotarev and semisimple-character comparison
QX-CHEBOTAREV.reference: J.S.Milne, Algebraic Number Theory, Theorem8.31; finite-dimensional semisimple character criterion.
QX-CHEBOTAREV.statement: Each conjugacy class in a finite Galois group occurs at infinitely many unramified primes; continuous semisimple characteristic-zero representations agreeing on a dense Frobenius set are isomorphic.
QX-CHEBOTAREV.matching: QX4 uses a class fixing the original F and K to obtain degree-one split auxiliary primes avoiding any finite set. QX1/QX9 check continuity and semisimplicity before comparison.

QX-AC.name: Cyclic cuspidal base change and descent with strong local compatibility
QX-AC.reference: Arthur--Clozel, Simple Algebras, Base Change, and the Advanced Theory of the Trace Formula, ChapterIII Theorem4.2(a),(b),(d), pp202--203; Theorem5.1, p212; ChapterI Section6, including Theorem6.2.
QX-AC.statement: A Galois-invariant cusp descends through a cyclic prime-degree extension, uniquely up to its finite quotient characters; a cusp base changes cuspidally unless the prescribed quotient self-twist occurs; global base change is strong at every place and compatible with the local correspondence.
QX-AC.matching: Only rank4 cyclic steps are used in QX9. Invariance follows from the actual extended r and strong multiplicity one. Irreducibility and the fresh ramified prime exclude exceptional self-twists. Every finite character ambiguity is corrected before returning the original r.

QX-HLTT.name: Galois existence without a prior polarization
QX-HLTT.reference: Harris--Lan--Taylor--Thorne, On the rigid cohomology of certain Shimura varieties, TheoremA / Corollary7.14.
QX-HLTT.statement: A regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GLn over a CM field has a continuous semisimple Galois representation matching geometric normalized unramified Satake polynomials.
QX-HLTT.matching: Used only after Arthur--Clozel constructs a specific descent cusp. Its restriction is the given irreducible r, so the finite-character discrepancy is explicitly removed. No automorphy of an arbitrary representation is inferred.

QX-CAR.name: Full CSD local compatibility and every-finite-place temperedness
QX-CAR.reference: A.Caraiani, Duke Math.J.161(2012), Theorems1.1--1.2, printedp2312; Monodromy and local-global compatibility for l=p, Theorem1.1 (ANT8(2014)).
QX-CAR.statement: For any n>=2 and actual cohomological conjugate-self-dual CM cusp, full Frobenius-semisimplified local compatibility holds at every finite place, and every finite local component is tempered.
QX-CAR.matching: QX9 applies only to the actual end2 CSD cusp at the chosen CM field, after the regular-algebraic/cohomological match. It then transports essential temperedness through the explicit cyclic chain. No Shin-regularity hypothesis is dropped from a theorem that has one.

QX-BGP.name: Semisimplified local compatibility at ell
QX-BGP.reference: Barnet-Lamb--Gee--Geraghty--Taylor, Local-global compatibility for l=p, II, TheoremA; Theorem1.1 and Corollary1.2.
QX-BGP.statement: At ell, the semisimplified Weil representation attached to an actual regular algebraic polarized CM cusp agrees with geometric local Langlands. Full Frobenius-semisimplification in this theorem has a further Shin-regularity condition.
QX-BGP.matching: QX9 uses only the first conclusion. Its equation QX.26 and literal Unl1 rule out norm-ratio monodromy entries, so N=0 is proved independently, then temperedness gives PotUnl and WinAt.

QX-CLOZEL.name: Regular algebraic cuspidal representations are cohomological
QX-CLOZEL.reference: L.Clozel, Motifs et formes automorphes (1990), Lemma3.14, with Theorem3.13; already matched in CX-CL.
QX-CLOZEL.statement: A regular C-algebraic cuspidal representation of GLn has nonzero relative Lie algebra cohomology with the algebraic coefficient of the same infinitesimal character.
QX-CLOZEL.matching: Matches the source IsRegAlg of the actual CSD cusp to Caraiani's cohomological premise. Only this archimedean consequence is reused; no counting or rationality bound is used.

QX-LINEAR.name: Finite-dimensional density, Clifford theory and elementary character independence
QX-LINEAR.reference: P.Etingof et al., Introduction to Representation Theory, Theorem2.5(i), p24; elementary proofs of the needed finite-index and self-twist cases are supplied in QX8--QX9.
QX-LINEAR.statement: A finite-dimensional irreducible representation over an algebraically closed field spans the full endomorphism algebra; distinct one-dimensional characters are linearly independent.
QX-LINEAR.matching: Burnside gives the trace-coordinate and weak-relation upgrades. QX8 proves the exact rank4 char-ell N3 argument, including characteristic3, rather than importing a stronger residual-image theorem.

QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.name: Noetherian local dimension and going-down facts
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.reference: Normal-domain going-down for integral extensions, the equality of regular-local dimension and cotangent dimension, and Krull intersection; the finite-point and formal-series comparison is already DX5.
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.statement: Integral finite domain extensions of a normal domain satisfy going-down; dimension is at most embedding dimension; equality characterizes a regular local ring, which is a domain; ideals of a complete Noetherian local ring are closed.
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.matching: QX2 uses normality of the actual regular weight ring and torsion-freeness before applying the dimension bound. It proves the support conclusion by localization. QX6 takes closed-ideal limits only in the complete Noetherian ring B.
QX-LOCAL-ALGEBRA.kind: standard commutative-algebra input with the needed argument given in the human proof
